chunks: Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurarah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام, who said:
"The owned slave, his divorce is not valid, nor his marriage, except with the permission of his master." I said: "Then if the master had married him off, in whose hand is the divorce?" He said:
"In the hand of the master: ‘Allah sets forth a parable: an owned slave who has no power over anything’—and the ‘thing’ is divorce."

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ: with the permission or authorization of
key_terms.سَيِّدِهِ: his master; the legal owner with authority over him
key_terms.طَلَاقُهُ: his divorce; the act of dissolving marriage attributed to him
key_terms.عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا: an owned servant/slave used in the Qur’anic parable
key_terms.لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ: having no authority or power over anything
key_terms.ٱلطَّلَاقُ: divorce; the legal dissolution of marriage
key_terms.ٱلْمَمْلُوكُ: an owned slave; a person under legal ownership

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority over the divorce of a slave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a slave’s marriage and divorce are not independently valid without the permission of his master. It also cites the Qur’anic example of an owned slave lacking authority over affairs, applying that meaning here specifically to the matter of divorce.
